item.title: Plume 0.19.0
item.description:
### New
- Bundle Plume's agent skills, and offer to install them from Home - Teach agents to use `plume`, `plume devices`, `plume wt`, and `plume stack` - Get Beta updates through Settings > Updates > Update source - Update using the built-in updater, even when installed via Homebrew - See subagents and background work on Home, as chips on each item - Update rendering of plans and subagent transcripts to share the chat's renderer - This means all improvement to the main chat like copy/paste across items, link chips for GitHub/Linear, etc. all work in plans and subagents - Improve Android device tabs - Pair a phone over Wi-Fi with a QR code or pairing code - Render emulators on the GPU, using about 95% less CPU - Copy/paste with the Mac clipboard into any device tab - Fold and unfold foldable emulators from the tab - Lower a physical device's video quality on a slow connection - Use less memory/CPU when streaming physical devices - Allow agents to specify phone/tablet/foldable instead of a specific model when reserving remote devices - Make the info pane clearer - Show all PRs in the same section - List all check statuses for a given PR - Copy a Linear issue's link from its row - Add the extended color palette, and match Home's sun and moon to your theme - Misc fixes - Polish the composer - Keep code blocks and text inside list items, indented like CommonMark - Paste a URL over selected text to link it - Show a tooltip on file chips with the file's full path - Show new project/worktree/folder options at the top of their dropdowns - ⌘⇧H opens Home - On Home, choosing a group picks its project - Mark a task unread when its terminal rings the bell - Stop agents from outliving Plume after a crash - Fix a rare transcript issue when an agent moves into a worktree
### Recently
- Add Home page, to keep track of all your chats - Add `plume devices`, to manage Android devices and emulators for agents - Host Android emulators, physical devices, and remote devices in a tab - Mention Linear issues, pull requests, and files in the composer with `@` and `#` - Add the `plume` command-line tool, with `plume wt` and `plume stack`
